method.build_seconds: Wall clock around the builder subprocess (`phase5g_profile_sheets.py --synthetic`), process start to exit: imports, DuckDB queries over the three parquets, writing out every sentence, compressing and writing the store, hashing it for the stamp.
method.store_mb: Sum of the bytes of every store file (index, parts, stamp), MB = 10^6 bytes.
method.lookup: 1000 keys drawn uniformly (seed 14) from all sheet keys. Each in its own new Python process: import the reader, open the store (`verify()`: read the stamp, SHA-256 every file, load the index), then time `get(level, code)` alone with perf_counter. `get_ms` is the lookup; `open_ms` is the one-off open a service pays once at start, reported separately. The OS file cache is warm after the first process (the store is read by each open's hash pass).
method.memory: psutil RSS in the same fresh process: after importing the reader, before opening; and after `verify()` plus one `get()`. The difference is the memory added by opening the store and reading one sheet. Median and maximum over the lookup processes.
